properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:19PM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 1 to 2.5 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 30 to 40 mph southwest
winds with gusts up to 40 to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT Wednesday, highest water levels expected
during each upcoming high tide through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
Wednesday morning as a series of low pressure systems track
across the Bering Sea. Coastal erosion and minor coastal
flooding will be possible with each upcoming high tide due to
the persistent onshore winds, during which maximum water levels
will reach between 1 and 2.5 ft above the normal highest tide
line, including in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. The
strong winds may reduce the ability for flood waters to recede
during and close to low tide, possibly leading to prolonged
higher than normal water levels along the coast and near the
mouth of the Kuskokwim River. There will be a break in strong
winds between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning,
however, we are monitoring the potential for another strong
storm system that could cause additional coastal impacts towards
the end of this week.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 25 at 12:56PM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok, and
Bethel.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 10 AM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southwest winds will become strong and gusty
by this afternoon. Winds are expected to be strongest along the
coast, but gusts as high as 55 mph are expected to persist inland
up to Bethel. Strongest winds are expected late tonight, and winds
will begin to diminish through Monday morning. However, steady
southwesterly flow is expected to continue into midweek.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 25 at 11:53AM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations of
3 to 6 inches. South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Central Brooks Range and Atigun Pass.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
will significantly reduce visibility to below one half mile with
areas below one quarter mile at times. Travel will be impacted
especially for high-profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will downslope on the northern side of
the Brooks Range, raising temperatures above freezing and reducing
snow amounts.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.
